stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // F10 LIGHTRUNNER / SKYDIO

//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Autonomous long-range flight

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give responders a live aerial view over distances of miles, where quadcopters fall short.

Why: Skydio says a single MegaDock, with F10's 30-mile flight radius, can put nearly 3,000 square miles within reach of one launch location.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: Deploying to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio's F10 Lightrunner is its first fixed-wing aircraft, built for emergency response, search and rescue, and asset inspection missions measured in miles. The company says it can launch in seconds, fly at speeds up to 100 mph, and use a robotic takeoff and landing system with no ground crew required. MegaDock, the dock for F10, will house up to five aircraft so a team can run concurrent missions.

Skydio also announced Asset Command and Security Command software platforms, which are available to purchase now with general availability early next year, along with Controller 2 and new camera and low-light capabilities for the existing X10 fleet. F10 is scheduled to deploy to customers in 2027.

Source: Skydio, Inc., 2026-09-24

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

BOATS THAT STAY
OUT FOR MONTHS

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, across open water.

Why: Crewed patrols are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and the area one asset can cover at a time.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish fleet deployed in the Gulf of America, per Seasats. Earlier Lightfish vessels operated on the Rio Grande from January 2026 in support of federal border security efforts.

Each Lightfish is about 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. It is solar powered, has multi-month endurance on station, and can be launched and recovered by two people. Its payload bay can be fitted with electro-optical and infrared cameras, signals gear or sonar, so one hull can be set up for different sensing jobs.

Seasats said the fleet was launched from the Texas coast and will conduct persistent surveillance in the Gulf of America. The work extends an autonomous surveillance effort the company says it supported for federal agencies on the southern border, and Seasats also reports more than $100 million in U.S. government contracts.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, Oct. 2, 2026

MISSION BRIEF // EAGLEEYE / ANDURIL

//Anduril Industries

📍Costa Mesa, CA

Tech: Digital vision

Platform: Warfighter augment headset

Goal: Give operators AI-enhanced sensing, threat detection and connectivity while they keep their eyes up and on the move.

Why: Overlaid spatial data and threat alerts are meant to help operators act before they are seen.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: Product page only; no test, purchase or fielding status stated in source.

EagleEye is a family of warfighter augments powered by Lattice, Anduril's software platform. Per the product page, the system combines Blue Force tracking, 6DOF spatial awareness, RF signature detection, rearview cameras and real-time battlefield alerts. Operators can task unmanned vehicles, call for fires and control robotic teammates, and a collaborative 3D sand table supports remote mission planning and rehearsal.

Source: Anduril Industries, product page (publish date not stated).

Image: Anduril (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE BLOCK 2C+RM

//Raytheon

📍Tucson, AZ

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Interceptor effector

Goal: Defeat current and emerging drone threats with an upgraded Coyote interceptor.

Why: A rocket motor is meant to speed launch, flight and successive shots.

Ticker: NYSE: RTX

Traction: Three Raytheon-funded developmental tests completed, per Raytheon.

Raytheon, an RTX business, completed three developmental tests of the Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrade, which it says moved the program from concept to testing in 15 months. The effort is Raytheon-funded and is meant to support an urgent joint U.S. military mission against evolving drone threats.

The upgrade adds a rocket motor for faster launch and flight, plus a new seeker and warhead. Raytheon says the initial series also confirmed early integration with the current counter-drone architecture. The current Coyote variants, which the company says have intercepted hundreds of drones, are the base for the upgrade.

The tests are developmental, and the source does not state a fielding date for Block 2C+RM.

Source: RTX, October 12, 2026

Image: RTX (courtesy)
